chunks: And Our command is but one (word), swift as the winking of an eye.

key_terms.لَمْحٍ: a glance / winking of an eye

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'swift as the winking of an eye' signify in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Qaf: 50) is often interpreted not merely as a description of divine power, but as a contrast to the gradual creation of the universe, emphasizing that God's command is singular and instantaneous, unlike the multiplicity of human perception. Scholars highlight that 'one command' (kalam-hin) signifies the absolute unity of the Divine Will, where no intermediate causes or delays exist in the execution of His decree. This immediacy serves as a reminder of the ease with which God can resurrect the dead or enact judgment, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid in action.
